card.name: Drug-interaction wording before effect verbs
card.fires_on: The word just before a verb of effect in drug-interaction text, such as the end of digoxin or reserpine, or the words inhibitors, have or more. Also seen in the same sentence slots in general science text.

modes.label: End of interacting drug name
modes.description: Last piece of a drug name that is the subject of an interaction statement.
modes.example: The concomitant use of naproxen with digox<<in>> has been reported to increase the serum concentration

modes.label: Inhibitor as subject
modes.description: The word inhibitors or an enzyme-inhibitor phrase starting an interaction statement.
modes.example: Moderate CYP3A4<< inhibitors>>: Recommended dosage is 21 mg

modes.label: Linking word in a relative clause
modes.description: A verb or adverb such as have or more following a subject in explanatory science prose.
modes.example: which<< have>> become a critical tool for investigating gene function

card.writes: Little clear effect; the promoted tokens are mostly Chinese words about need and cause.
card.plain: It fires on the word right before the sentence says what an interacting drug does or causes.
